samples.summary: setBlockType on a table block inserts a stray inline node as the table node's first child, shifting every row index — the new test exercises exactly this call and only passes because the reader filters children by type 'row'
samples.evidence: The delta adds `store.setBlockType(tableBlock.id, 'table')` (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, 'should not strip list/heading attrs from blocks nested in its cells'). In setBlockType, after the styleByPath/removeNodeStyle writes, the `else if (block.inlines.length === 0)` branch at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469 runs for any non-HR/page-break type; a table block always has `inlines: []` (treeNodeToBlock:443), so `tree.editByPath([...blockPath,0],[...blockPath,0], buildInlineNode({text:'',style:{}}))` inserts an `inline` element as child 0 of the TABLE node. Nothing filters that out on write. Read-back hides it (treeNodeToBlock:432 keeps only `c.type === 'row'`), so the new assertions pass — but the CRDT tree now has rows at child indices 1..n while `findBlockInTable`/`resolveBlockTreePath` (lines 791-813, 820) address a cell block as `[...tablePath, rowIdx, cellIdx, blockIdx]`, i.e. row r at child index r. Any subsequent edit to a cell of that table therefore targets the wrong tree node (off by one) or the stray inline. The guard `if (type === 'horizontal-rule' || type === 'page-break')` should also exclude `type === 'table'` (and any block carrying tableData).

samples.summary: toHeadingStyleId drops <w:pStyle> for headingLevel 7-9, which the DOCX importer can legitimately produce, losing round-trip fidelity that the previous code preserved
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:137 matches `/^(?:Heading|heading)(\d)$/` and stores `headingLevel = parseInt(...)` without clamping, so importing a Word document with `Heading7`/`Heading8`/`Heading9` (or a Korean numeric style id `7`) yields headingLevel 7-9. The old exporter emitted `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading7"/>` verbatim (harmless and round-trippable); the new `toHeadingStyleId` rejects anything >6 and returns undefined, so the paragraph exports with no pStyle at all and re-importing it produces a plain paragraph rather than a heading. Clamping to 6 (as `named-styles.ts:108` already does for rendering) would keep both the injection-proofness and the fidelity.

samples.summary: Theme colors that toRgbHexColor cannot express now silently export as black instead of their approximate value — a theme whose `background` slot holds a CSS color name or an empty string yields an all-black PPTX color scheme
samples.evidence: `toSrgbHex` was `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`; it is now `toRgbHexColor(hex) ?? '000000'`. `toRgbHexColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:113) returns undefined for named CSS colors ('white'), `var(--…)`, empty strings and fully transparent values. Unlike every other sink using it, a clrScheme slot cannot be dropped, so those degrade to #000000 — e.g. a `background: 'white'` theme (possible via a hand-written/PUT theme or a future token that is not a hex literal) exports as a black background for text that is also black. All in-tree themes are 6-digit hex so this does not fire today; a clamp/fallback to the corresponding default-light role value would be safer than black.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. yorkie-doc-store.ts:1462 guards only 'horizontal-rule'/'page-break'; the else-branch at :1469 runs for type 'table' and inserts an inline element node (buildInlineNode, :305-314) as child 0 of the table block node via tree.editByPath([...blockPath,0],[...blockPath,0],...). A table block always satisfies block.inlines.length === 0 (treeNodeToBlock returns inlines: [] at :443; createTableBlock sets inlines: [] at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:531), and `block` is the table block itself (getBlockByRegion, :1413). Read-back hides the stray node because treeNodeToBlock filters children to c.type === 'row' (:432), which is exactly why the new test's assertions (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1990-1998) still pass. Writes, however, address rows positionally: findBlockInTable returns [r,c,b] (:791-813), resolveBlockTreePath composes [...tablePath, r, c, b] (:820, :842-845), and getTreeBlockNode walks raw children[idx] (:864-870) — so after the insert, row r is at child index r+1 and any subsequent cell edit targets the wrong node or dereferences the childless inline and throws. No caller-side guard exists: Document.setBlockType (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:453-464) passes the id through unchecked, and editor.ts:3036 / text-box-editor.ts:1178 pass cursor.position.blockId; the store API is also called directly by the new test. MemStore's equivalent logic (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:260-264) is harmless because it only touches a JS array, confirming the Yorkie tree write is the defect. Real CRDT structural corruption / crash path — in the correctness lane and blocking.

finding.summary: The new slides-arm block walker validates block styles but not inline entries, so a PUT can still store a slide text block whose `inlines[i].text` is missing/non-string — which throws inside the docs layout engine for every viewer
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (controller.ts:683-720) checks only `block.style` and recurses into `tableData`. The docs arm added exactly the opposite guard for the same `Block` shape — 'buildInlineNode reads inline.text.length … an element missing either turns a malformed PUT into a 500' (controller.ts:422-442). Slide text bodies are persisted verbatim as JSON by `writeSlidesRoot`, then laid out by the SAME docs engine: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:286` does `const len = inline.text.length` and 289/290 `inline.text.slice(...)`. A payload of `{slides:[{…,elements:[{id,type:'text',frame:{},data:{blocks:[{style:{},inlines:[{}]}]}}]}]}` is accepted, and thereafter `computeLayout` throws a TypeError on every render of that slide (all viewers), not just a 400 for the caller. The stated round-trip rationale only justifies tolerating *omitted* `id`/`inlines`, not an inline entry with a non-string `text`.

verdict.reason: The slides-arm walker does validate inline entries. `assertValidSlideBlocks` calls `assertValidSlideInlines(block.inlines, ...)` at docs-content.controller.ts:704 — inside the exact 683-720 range the finding quotes as checking "only block.style and tableData". `assertValidSlideInlines` (:741-770) rejects a non-array `inlines` (:743), a non-object entry (:750), a non-string `inline.text` (:755-758, the precise guard claimed missing), and a non-object `inline.style` (:760-767). The reviewer's example payload `{elements:[{type:'text',data:{blocks:[{style:{},inlines:[{}]}]}}]}` therefore yields a 400, not a stored deck: PUT → assertValidSlidesBody (:153) → assertValidSlide (:481) → assertValidElement (:553) → assertValidElementData (:580,:619) → assertValidTextBodyBlocks (:675) → assertValidSlideBlocks (:704) → assertValidSlideInlines, where `inline.text === undefined` trips :755. The other ingress paths for the same Block shape are covered by the same walk: slide `notes` (:557), layout placeholders/staticElements (:513 → assertValidNestedElement :599 → assertValidElementData), group children (:639), shape/table cell bodies (:623,:633), and nested docs-table cells inside a slide text body (:714). The function's own doc comment (:723-740) states the identical rationale the finding says was never applied on the slides side.
